reviewRequired.note: The Sun is the intended source for this photosynthesis-based classroom web. “All food webs” is too broad: some are based on chemosynthesis.

A is intended: silver perch, trout and pelican can occupy third-consumer positions along appropriate paths. The omnivorous network allows more than one trophic position; do not treat each organism as having one fixed level.
B is intended in the historical five-kingdom model. Classification systems differ; the model must be specified.
C is the narrow intended effect: foxes eat introduced rabbits. This does not establish a net ecological benefit of fox introduction; native predation can outweigh it.
The Sun is the intended source for this photosynthesis-based classroom web. “All food webs” is too broad: some are based on chemosynthesis.
B is intended as least specifically linked to cold or fast swimming, but swallowing prey whole can still aid feeding/survival; comparison is subjective.
An additional open-response sentence precedes the true/false task but has no printed mark allocation. Proposed2-mark rubric is clearly separate from the printed42-mark paper total.
Source includes inline T/F answers. These are removed from the student prompt; itemd uses simplified conservation-category wording.
Inline source answer MUTUALISM contradicts its own stem. Corrected to commensalism; retain manual review.
